claims.text: Coupling high-throughput AIMD with CALPHAD and experimental calibration can predict thermophysical properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The coupled approach can predict HEA melting temperatures with approximately 5–10% accuracy.
The coupled approach can predict HEA enthalpies of fusion with approximately 5–10% accuracy.
The coupled approach can predict HEA entropies of fusion with approximately 5–10% accuracy.
The coupled approach can predict volume changes at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
AIMD simulations spanning temperatures from ambient conditions to above the expected melting point can capture the melting process.
Integrating CALPHAD with AIMD can extend predictions across HEA compositional space.
Sufficiently large supercells and extended simulation times are required to capture melting dynamics accurately.
Temperature-ramp protocols mimicking equilibrium conditions will improve the accuracy of melting predictions.
Changes in structure factors and radial distribution functions identify the transition from crystalline order to liquid disorder.
Atomic-structure analysis can indicate melting and associated volume changes.
AIMD captures the atomic interactions and dynamical changes occurring during HEA melting.
Energy differences computed during order–disorder transitions can be used to estimate latent heat.
Energy differences computed during order–disorder transitions can be used to estimate entropy changes.
CALPHAD refines AIMD-derived predictions and generalizes them across compositional space.
The AIMD–CALPHAD workflow can provide liquid-phase thermodynamic predictions in a high-throughput manner.
Predictive accuracy may deteriorate for compositions well outside the experimental calibration range.
Severe atomic-size mismatch may reduce predictive accuracy because simulation limitations become more pronounced.
Finite cell sizes, limited simulation times, and calibration errors are sources of predictive uncertainty.
A deviation greater than 10% between prediction and experiment for any targeted melting property would rule out the proposed approach.
